clue.text: Professional model, the toast of Berlin

blocks.note: a pro is a professional
to model for an artist is to sit for them

explanation.surface: A professional model is the toast of Berlin, the most celebrated figure in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toast' looks like fame, but it is literal: the answer is the German drinking salute.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosit is the German word said when raising glasses, the equivalent of 'cheers'.

clue.text: Careless about energy and power to begin with in building

indicators.note: about means going around, so one word is wrapped around another
to begin with places this piece at the very front of the rest

blocks.note: P is the standard abbreviation for power
remiss means negligent or careless
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone is careless with energy and power use when starting work in a building.
explanation.walkthrough: The energy letter goes before the final S, not around the whole word; 'to begin with' puts the power letter at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Premises are the land and buildings a business occupies, so a building is an example.

clue.text: Violent attack where shooting takes place

blocks.note: first meaning: an onslaught or assault
second meaning, split as two words: the place where a film is shot

explanation.surface: A violent attack occurs at the scene of a shooting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shooting' suggests guns, but it is filming: read the answer as ON SET.
explanation.definitionFit: An onset is an assault, and actors filming are 'on set', the stage where cameras roll.

clue.text: Knock pub sign askew

indicators.note: something askew is out of line, so these letters are set crooked into a new order

blocks.note: an inn is a pub
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone knocks a pub sign so that it hangs crooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knock' looks like a verb, but in cricket a knock is a batsman's spell at the crease.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket slang a knock is a batter's innings, the period they spend batting.

clue.text: European surrounded by throng was exultant

indicators.note: surrounded by means enclosed on all sides by the other word

blocks.note: a throng is a crowd
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A European fan in the middle of a throng celebrated wildly.
explanation.definitionFit: To crow is to boast or gloat triumphantly, so someone who crowed was exultant.

clue.text: Determination of tragic lovers, what Romeo and Juliet have in common

indicators.note: a tragic ending leaves things wrecked, so these letters are broken and rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

blocks.clueFragment: what Romeo and Juliet have in common
blocks.note: the only letter found in both names Romeo and Juliet

explanation.surface: The determination of Shakespeare's doomed couple is something Romeo and Juliet share.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What they have in common' sounds like a shared trait, but it means the shared letter of the two names.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolve is firmness of purpose, a synonym for determination.

clue.text: Crime story that has errors in grammar and spelling

definitions.text: Crime story that has errors in grammar and spelling

blocks.note: surface reading: a detective novel

blocks.clueFragment: that has errors in grammar and spelling
blocks.note: setter's reading: the genre's informal name is a slangy, misspelt question asking who committed the crime

explanation.surface: A badly edited crime novel is full of grammatical and spelling mistakes.
explanation.walkthrough: The name comes from 'Who done it?', where 'done' should be 'did' and the spelling is further mangled.
explanation.definitionFit: A whodunnit is a detective story whose puzzle is identifying the culprit.

clue.text: Contributing to aid, we'll save lives

indicators.note: contributing to means supplying a part of the following words rather than all of them

blocks.note: the letters run across these words, ignoring punctuation

explanation.surface: By donating to an aid charity, we will help save lives.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell somewhere is to live there, so 'dwells' means 'lives' in the residing sense.

clue.text: For each child, a line that's derogatory

blocks.note: per means for each
a son is a child
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: Every child is given a line of insulting remarks.
explanation.definitionFit: A personal remark attacks someone's character or looks, so it is insulting and derogatory.

clue.text: African imprisoning sailor who's opposed to oppressive government?

indicators.note: imprisoning means holding something inside, so one word is locked within another

blocks.note: a Liberian is someone from Liberia in West Africa
tar is old slang for a sailor

explanation.surface: An African regime jails a sailor who campaigns against tyranny.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition as loose: a libertarian opposes state interference generally.
explanation.definitionFit: A libertarian champions individual liberty and wants minimal state power over citizens.

clue.text: Fabrication's sound for part of house

indicators.note: a word's sound is how it is heard when spoken, not how it is written

blocks.note: a fabrication is a made-up story, a lie

explanation.surface: A builder's made-up excuse sounds plausible enough for one part of a house.
explanation.definitionFit: A storey is one floor or level of a building, such as the upstairs.

clue.text: Very easy clue, for example, provided in good time

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the pair of letters that follow

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
provided, as in 'provided that', means if
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A very easy clue, for instance, delivered promptly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In good time' reads as 'early', but it splits into G and T with the conditional word placed between.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything so easy it needs no effort is called a gift, and a simple clue is one example.

clue.text: In way that's not clear, you'll be upset with Sun

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disturbed, so these letters fall into a different order

blocks.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe
taken as written

explanation.surface: A vague warning that you'll be upset by a story in the Sun newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The upset fodder is 'you'll be' plus 'Sun'; 'with' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Nebulous means hazy or vague, so acting nebulously is acting in an unclear, indistinct way.

clue.text: New money to encourage specialist in theatre

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
euros are the currency of much of Europe
to urge on is to encourage

explanation.surface: New funding is offered to encourage a specialist working in the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Theatre' suggests the stage, but here it is the operating theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A neurosurgeon is a surgeon specialising in brain and nerve operations, performed in an operating theatre.

clue.text: Buttress supporting church — it's under control

indicators.note: in a down entry, being under something means coming below it, so this part follows the other

blocks.note: to rein is to control, as with a horse
to be for something is to support it
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A buttress holds up a church, keeping its structure under control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporting church' forms the lower half, sitting under the word for control in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To buttress something is to strengthen or prop it up, which is what reinforce means.

clue.text: Study to be a fighter, and keep in good shape

blocks.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn
to serve is to be in the armed forces

explanation.surface: Someone trains to become a fighter and stays physically fit.
explanation.definitionFit: To conserve is to preserve or protect from harm, keeping something in good condition.

clue.text: Military establishment at Waterloo, say, with everyone inside

indicators.note: inside means placed within, so this word sits in the middle of the other

blocks.note: at and in both mean located at a place
Waterloo is a London railway station; 'say' marks it as an example
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A military base at Waterloo, the battlefield, with all the troops gathered within.
explanation.walkthrough: Waterloo suggests Wellington's battle, but here it is the London railway station.
explanation.definitionFit: An installation is a military base or facility, an establishment for armed forces.

clue.text: Realise achievement you see replicated, we hear, in offspring

indicators.note: we hear means the words are taken by how they come across when spoken
in places one piece inside the word that follows

blocks.note: seed is an old word for offspring or descendants
the second word is said twice, and each word is heard as a single letter

explanation.surface: Parents see their own achievement copied in their children.
explanation.walkthrough: The spoken letters U, C, C go between the first S and the EED of SEED.
explanation.definitionFit: To succeed is to accomplish what one set out to do, realising an achievement.

clue.text: Descent needing rope and lot of time

blocks.note: a line is a rope or cord
an age is a long time

explanation.surface: A slow climb down a cliff requires rope and plenty of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Descent' suggests abseiling, but it means ancestry.
explanation.definitionFit: Lineage is ancestry, the line of descent from one's forebears.

clue.text: Great intelligence information on one world power, initially

blocks.note: gen is British slang for information
I is the Roman numeral for one
the initials of the United States, a world power

explanation.surface: Top-level intelligence information about one world power has come in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intelligence' suggests spying, which the surface encourages; it is the definition, meaning brainpower.
explanation.definitionFit: Genius is exceptional intellectual ability, so it means great intelligence.

clue.text: What's ideal for nice pet is being spoiled

indicators.note: something being spoiled is ruined, so these letters are wrecked and rebuilt

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The ideal state for a nice pet is to be pampered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoiled' reads as pampered, which suits a pet; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Perfection is the ideal, the state of being flawless.

clue.text: It's engaged setter and solver in past

indicators.note: in places one pair of people inside the word that follows

blocks.note: by means past, as in walking by
the setter and solver together are 'us'

explanation.surface: The setter and solver were once engaged to each other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engaged' suggests betrothal, but it is a phone line in use.
explanation.definitionFit: A busy telephone line is one that is engaged, already in use.

clue.text: Vessel in dock

blocks.note: first meaning: a bowl for holding liquid
second meaning: an enclosed area of water where ships moor

explanation.surface: A ship lies in dock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship, which fits the dock; it is a bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: A basin is both a bowl for washing and an enclosed harbour area where boats are berthed.

clue.text: Break through, with knight or bishop, say, capturing rook or queen

indicators.note: capturing means taking and holding, so one word holds the letter inside

blocks.note: knights and bishops are examples of chess pieces
R stands for rook in chess notation and for Regina, queen

explanation.surface: A chess player breaks through using a knight or bishop to take a rook or queen.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce is to penetrate or puncture, making a way through.

clue.text: Rescue craft with no shortage of mates

definitions.text: Rescue craft with no shortage of mates

blocks.note: surface reading: a lifeboat
setter's reading: the biblical boat that saved every animal in breeding pairs

explanation.surface: A lifeboat with a full crew of first mates and second mates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mates' suggests ship's officers, but it means animal partners, which boarded two by two.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, the vessel saved one family and pairs of every creature from the Flood.

clue.text: Firm modified ads yet otherwise stayed disorganised

indicators.note: something modified has been altered, so these letters change their order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A company altered its adverts, yet otherwise remained chaotic.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue offers two routes: 'otherwise' introduces a second anagram, 'stayed disorganised', which gives the same letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Steady means stable and fixed, as firm does.

clue.text: Some may come late to this meeting, possibly creating a scene

definitions.text: Some may come late to this meeting

indicators.note: possibly means in one of several possible arrangements, so these letters may be reordered

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Latecomers to a meeting may cause a fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Late' means dead, not tardy: the deceased are summoned at this gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A séance is a meeting held to contact the spirits of dead people, 'the late'.
